title: Affine inverse limits of spaces and eventual schematicity
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $I$ be a small nonempty directed set, and let $(Z_i)_{i\in I}$ be an inverse system of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] with affine transition morphisms. A space is quasi-compact if it admits a surjective etale chart from a quasi-compact scheme, and quasi-separated if its diagonal is quasi-compact, where a map is quasi-compact if its inverse image over every affine scheme test is quasi-compact. A morphism is affine if it is representable and its pullback to every affine scheme test has affine source. The limit $Z=\varprojlim_i Z_i$ of the associated fppf sheaves is an algebraic space and each projection $q_i:Z\to Z_i$ is affine. If all $Z_i$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated, then: if $Z$ is a scheme, some $Z_i$ is a scheme; if $Z$ is an affine scheme, some $Z_i$ is an affine scheme. In either case all later stages have the same property. For any $i$ and any morphism of algebraic spaces $W\to Z_i$, one has $Z\times_{Z_i}W\cong\varprojlim_{j\geq i}(Z_j\times_{Z_i}W)$.

source.place: Tags 07SF (lemma-directed-inverse-system-has-limit), 07SQ (lemma-limit-is-affine), and 07SR (lemma-limit-is-scheme); the latter two use Situation 084R (situation-descent).

proof.text: Fix $0\in I$ and restrict to the cofinal directed tail $i\ge0$. Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $U_0\to Z_0$ and set $R_0=U_0\times_{Z_0}U_0$. Its two projections are etale and $R_0$ is a scheme. Put $U_i=Z_i\times_{Z_0}U_0$ and $R_i=Z_i\times_{Z_0}R_0$. Since $Z_i\to Z_0$ is affine these are schemes; their transition maps are affine by base change. The scheme-limit theorem supplies schemes $U=\varprojlim U_i$ and $R=\varprojlim R_i$ with affine projections. The identities $R_i=U_i\times_{U_0}R_0$ with either projection show, by testing maps from any scheme, that $R=U\times_{U_0}R_0$ for either projection. Thus $s,t:R\rightrightarrows U$ are etale. Compatible pairs in the equivalence relations $R_i(T)$ form an equivalence relation on $U(T)$: reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity hold coordinatewise, and uniqueness makes the resulting witnesses compatible. Hence $R\to U\times_S U$ is an etale equivalence relation.

The quotient theorem gives an algebraic space $Q=U/R$ with $U\to Q$ surjective etale and $R=U\times_Q U$. The compatible maps $U\to U_i\to Z_i$ descend to $Q\to F:=\varprojlim_i Z_i$ as fppf sheaves. For a scheme $T$ and a compatible family $T\to Z_i$, the single etale cover $T\times_{Z_0}U_0\to T$ maps compatibly to every $U_i$, hence to $U$. Therefore $Q\to F$ is locally surjective. If two sections of $Q(T)$ have the same image, lift them fppf locally to $a,b:T\to U$. The equalities of their images in every $Z_i$ give unique $c_i:T\to R_i$ with projections $(a_i,b_i)$. Uniqueness forces compatibility, so $(c_i)$ gives $T\to R$ and the two quotient sections agree. Sheaf uniqueness descends this equality to $T$. Thus $Q\simeq F$, proving existence of the required algebraic space $Z$.

For any fixed $i$, carry out the same construction starting at $i$ to obtain $Z\times_{Z_i}U_i\simeq U$, where $U\to U_i$ is affine. The affine-locality lemma therefore makes $q_i:Z\to Z_i$ affine. For any $W\to Z_i$ and any test scheme $T$, a map $T\to Z\times_{Z_i}W$ is exactly a map $T\to W$ and a compatible tail family $T\to Z_j$ with the prescribed common map to $Z_i$. These are exactly compatible maps to $Z_j\times_{Z_i}W$. The resulting bijections commute with restriction in $T$, proving the displayed base-change isomorphism of sheaves, hence of algebraic spaces. Cofinality of the tail follows by sending a component at $j\ge i,k$ down to $k$; directedness makes this independent of $j$.

Assume now every $Z_i$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. As $q_0$ is affine, $Z$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by affine permanence. Suppose first $Z$ is affine and write $Z=\operatorname{Spec}A$. The finite-affine-atlas lemma allows $U_0$ in step 1 to be affine. All $U_i$ and $U$ are then affine and $U\to Z$ is surjective etale. Write $A_i=\Gamma(Z_i,\mathcal O_{Z_i})$ and $C_i=\Gamma(U_i,\mathcal O_{U_i})$; the space-sections lemma gives $A=\varinjlim A_i$, and scheme section continuity gives $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)=\varinjlim C_i$, with element representation and eventual equality. All these maps are the actual pullbacks, so the maps $A_i\to C_i$ are compatible.

source.place: Tags 07SQ (lemma-limit-is-affine) and 07SI (lemma-descend-section), choice of affine chart and rings

proof.text: Put $B=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$, so $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is surjective etale. Etale algebra descent along the ring colimit $A=\varinjlim A_i$ gives, after choosing and renaming a stage $0$, an etale $A_0$-algebra $B_0$ and a specified $A$-algebra isomorphism $A\otimes_{A_0}B_0\simeq B$. Put $B_i=A_i\otimes_{A_0}B_0$. These are etale by base change. Because both spectra are affine and the map is etale (locally of finite presentation), $B_0$ has a finite algebra presentation $A_0[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(g_1,\ldots,g_m)$, by the locally-finitely-presented affine-open lemma. The scheme descent-of-surjectivity lemma applied to $\operatorname{Spec}B_0\to\operatorname{Spec}A_0$ over the inverse system $\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ gives a stage after which every $\operatorname{Spec}B_i\to\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ is surjective. Its hypotheses hold: the three initial schemes are affine and hence qcqs, the morphism is locally finitely presented, and its limit is the given surjective map $U\to Z$.

source.place: Tag 07SQ (lemma-limit-is-affine), finite etale model and surjectivity; replaces the square-Jacobian coordinates by etale algebra descent

proof.text: Choose representatives in some $C_i$ for the images in $B$ of the finitely many generators $x_\nu$ of $B_0$. Each of the finitely many elements $g_\lambda(h_1,\ldots,h_n)$ has zero image in $B=\varinjlim C_i$, so after increasing $i$ all vanish. The quotient presentation now gives an $A_i$-algebra map $B_i\to C_i$ whose pullback is the specified identification with $B$. This defines $U_i\to\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ compatible with global functions from $Z_i$. For precision, the canonical map $Z_i\to\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ is constructed by restricting $A_i$ to a scheme atlas and using the scheme affine-target bijection. The two maps on the atlas overlap agree because their ring maps do; they descend uniquely as maps of fppf sheaves. This also proves functoriality of this canonical map and compatibility of the displayed square. These are finite-generator and sheaf-uniqueness arguments, with no assumption that $Z_i$ is a scheme.

source.place: Tag 07SQ (lemma-limit-is-affine), elements h and the displayed square; affine-target map as in spaces-properties.tex Tag 05Z1 (lemma-morphism-to-affine-scheme)

proof.text: Reindex at the stage of step 6 and set $T_0=Z_0\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A_0}\operatorname{Spec}B_0$. The square gives $g_0:U_0\to T_0$ over $Z_0$. Both $U_0\to Z_0$ and $T_0\to Z_0$ are representable etale, and $T_0\to Z_0$ is affine as the pullback of the affine morphism between the two affine spectra. Thus $U_0$ and $T_0$ are qcqs. The chartwise-etale permanence lemma applies to $U_0$ and $T_0$, both etale over $Z_0$, and says that $g_0$ is chartwise etale. On scheme charts it is therefore etale and hence locally of finite presentation by the definition of etale. At the limit $T_0\times_{Z_0}Z=\operatorname{Spec}(B_0\otimes_{A_0}A)=U$, and $g_0$ pulls back to the specified isomorphism of step 6. The representable-isomorphism descent lemma applies, giving some $i$ for which $U_i\simeq Z_i\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A_i}\operatorname{Spec}B_i$.

The cover $\operatorname{Spec}B_i\to\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ is surjective etale by step 5. Under the Cartesian square of step 7, its pullback of $Z_i\to\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ is $U_i\to\operatorname{Spec}B_i$, which is affine since both schemes are affine. Etale target locality for affine space morphisms implies $Z_i\to\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ is affine; in particular $Z_i$ is an affine scheme. This proves the affine-limit clause without assuming a schematic stage.

If $Z$ is merely a scheme, its quasi-compactness from step 4 gives a finite affine open cover $Z=\bigcup_{a=1}^n W_a$. Descend this cover by the open-cover descent lemma to quasi-compact quasi-separated opens $W_{a,i}\subset Z_i$ that cover $Z_i$. The base-change formula of step 3 identifies $W_a=\varprojlim_{j\ge i}W_{a,j}$; the transition maps are affine. Apply the affine-limit result proved in steps 4--8 to each of these finitely many systems. Directedness permits a common stage where every $W_{a,j}$ is affine: after an affine stage all later sources are affine by affine permanence. These affine scheme open subspaces cover $Z_j$, so the scheme representability criterion applies to its fppf sheaf, which is in particular a Zariski sheaf. The inclusions are representable open immersions and they cover on every scheme test. Therefore $Z_j$ is a scheme. If the cover is empty, the open-cover descent lemma gives an empty stage, represented by $\operatorname{Spec}0$.

source.place: Tag 07SR (lemma-limit-is-scheme), finite affine cover, including eventual covering condition

proof.text: Finally if $Z_i$ is a scheme then for $j\ge i$ the affine morphism $Z_j\to Z_i$ has a scheme source by affine representability. If $Z_i$ is affine, its affine source $Z_j$ is affine. This proves persistence of each property at every later stage.
